findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime keys, but the audit log endpoint uses it with order_by="-datetime"
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to getattr(item, self.key), copied from the numeric Paginator. The audit log endpoint instantiates it with order_by="-datetime", so the key value is a datetime object and math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime. get_item_key is called by build_cursor for every non-empty page (including the first page, via _build_next_values), so any request with optimized_pagination=true that returns at least one audit log row will 500. Additionally, value_from_cursor returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of converting it back to a datetime the way DateTimePaginator does, so even if get_item_key were fixed, subsequent pages would compare a timestamp column against a bare integer in the .extra(where=...) clause, causing a database error or wrong filtering. The paginator needs DateTimePaginator-style key/value handling, or the endpoint should not use it with a datetime ordering.

findings.title: "Advanced" negative-offset branch slices the queryset with a negative index, which Django rejects with ValueError
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is set and the incoming cursor has a negative offset, the code evaluates queryset[cursor.offset : cursor.offset + limit + extra] with a negative slice start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing — queryset[-10:5] raises ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported — so the request returns a 500. The inline comment claiming "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false. Negative offsets are client-controllable because Cursor.from_string accepts them (e.g. cursor=0:-10:0), while cursors produced by build_cursor never contain negative offsets, so this branch only ever triggers on hand-crafted cursors and only ever crashes. The advertised feature provides no working functionality; it should either be implemented against a real mechanism or removed, with negative offsets rejected up front.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None, causing AttributeError for token-authenticated requests
findings.body: For every non-superuser request the new code evaluates organization_context.member.has_global_access, but RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is None when the caller has no membership row — for example requests authenticated with an org auth token or API key carrying org:read scope, which legitimately pass OrganizationAuditPermission. The previous code never dereferenced member, so such requests now fail with AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access' and return a 500. Guard the access (e.g. organization_context.member is not None and organization_context.member.has_global_access) and decide explicitly whether token-authenticated callers may use the optimized path.

findings.title: No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized_pagination query parameter
findings.body: The PR adds a new ~100-line paginator class and a new endpoint branch selected via optimized_pagination=true, but adds no tests. Any test exercising the new path with actual results would have caught that it raises TypeError on datetime keys and that the negative-offset branch 500s. Add unit tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator (datetime ordering, cursor round-trips, is_prev handling) and endpoint tests covering both branches, including non-superuser members and token-authenticated callers.
